summary: This standards-track document extends the IANA IS-IS TLV Codepoints registry. The registry says which TLVs may appear in which PDUs but not which can appear in purges. This adds a record of permitted TLVs in purges and updates a related earlier specification.

plainLanguage.summary: IS-IS uses a purge to tell routers to discard an old link-state record. RFC 6233 adds registry information showing which TLVs may appear in purges and clarifies checks for authenticated purges.

questions: which tlvs are allowed in is-is purge
which tlvs allowed in is-is purge
subtitle: Adds purge-permission information to the IS-IS TLV registry and updates authentication rules.

tldr.problem: The IS-IS TLV Codepoints registry did not say which TLVs may appear in a purge, even though later authentication extensions allow some TLVs in purges.
tldr.mechanism: The registry gains a Purge column, and RFC 6233 updates how authenticated purges are generated, accepted, and propagated.
tldr.outcome: RFC 6233 updates RFC 3563, RFC 5304, and RFC 5310.

today: RFC 6233 is a Proposed Standard that updates RFC 3563, RFC 5304, and RFC 5310.

sections.title: What a Purge Contains
sections.content:
IS-IS floods Link State PDUs to maintain a link-state database. When information in an LSP is no longer needed, the purge mechanism causes routers in the domain to discard it. The original process retained the LSP header and discarded its TLVs.

Later authentication extensions changed how purges are generated and allowed certain TLVs to remain. The IANA registry did not record which TLVs were permitted in purges.
sections.plainLanguage: A purge tells other routers to discard an old LSP. Because extensions allow some metadata to remain in a purge, implementers need a list of which TLVs are allowed.

sections.title: The Purge Column in the Registry
sections.content: RFC 6233 adds a Purge column to the IS-IS TLV Codepoints registry. A y means a TLV may appear in a purge; an n means it must not. Initially, TLV type 10, Authentication, and type 137, Dynamic hostname, receive y; all other entries receive n. The status also applies to sub-TLVs of a TLV.
sections.plainLanguage: The new column marks each TLV as allowed or not allowed in a purge. At the start, Authentication and Dynamic hostname are marked as allowed.

sections.title: Generating and Checking Authenticated Purges
sections.content:
An implementation that supports authentication must reject a purge containing a TLV that the registry does not allow. It must also reject an unlisted TLV unless the purge contains the Purge Originator Identification (POI) TLV. A purge that is accepted must be propagated without removing TLVs. If an implementation adds a POI TLV to an accepted purge that lacked one, it must recompute authentication.

When generating an authenticated purge, the implementation removes TLVs not allowed by the registry, adds the POI TLV, may add other allowed TLVs, and then adds authentication. An LSP with non-zero Remaining Lifetime must not contain the POI TLV.
sections.plainLanguage: Routers check purge contents against the registry before accepting an authenticated purge. When building one, they remove disallowed TLVs, add the required POI TLV, and calculate authentication for the resulting message.

sections.title: Security and Status
sections.content: The RFC states that it introduces no new security issues. It updates RFC 3563, RFC 5304, and RFC 5310.
sections.plainLanguage: The memo clarifies registry and authentication behavior for IS-IS purges and reports no new security issues.
